title: The A(a, b) machine: the wiki's rules in Lean, and no congruence rules out the halt
text: For 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC, Lean now proves the eight rules on the tapes A(a, b) for all sizes, so the machine halts if and only if they lead from A(2, 9) to some A(a, 3). No b = 3 in the first 10<sup>8</sup> visits (native_decide), nor in 10<sup>12</sup> by C. A halt needs one visit A(a, a + 4) with a even; that class gets its full share of near-diagonal visits mod every modulus tried, and random starts halt by the same rule, so the halt looks like a rare random event (about 0.11 per decade of visits).
